items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Topics 97:1
items.html: (To the question) The Gevurot of the Nukva are not her own, for from herself she is rooted only in the Malchut of Ima, which is the second restriction, and no Mochin emerge upon her except by the inclusion of the Malchut of Ima in the crown of Gevura of ZA, as is known. Therefore she is the aspect of a soft Din, for all the Gevurot of the first restriction that are in her are only the aspect of an illumination that she receives from the Gevurot of ZA, as above. But ZA does not need to receive the illumination of Gevurot from another, for he receives the aspect of the Gevurot of the first restriction from his source, from the Mazal VeNotzer, which is the aspect of the Yesod of Malchut, from the first restriction, as is known. Therefore his NHY, which is the place of the end, are harsh Dinim, for the aspect of the first restriction is the measure of the harsh Din, in which the world cannot exist except with its partnership with the measure of mercy, as is known. Therefore, the further it goes, the Dinim grow in it, and his NHY have no sweetening except in their clothing in the Mochin of the Nukva, who is the aspect of the Malchut of Ima and the second restriction; and there they are sweetened in the measure of the mercy of Ima. (Item 112).
